notes: The distilled cheat-sheet did NOT lift the junior reviewer on this PR; it appears to have hurt recall. Both reviews caught the shift-state concern (candidate #3, baseline #1 -> GT 0). Beyond that, the DISTILLED (candidate) review anchored heavily on cheat-sheet themes it repeatedly cites verbatim (DPI coordinate-space docs, _showGeneration/visibility guards, surrogate-pair SendInput, VirtualizingStackPanel perf, multi-arch build evidence). Those are plausible-sounding but map to concerns the REAL reviewers never raised, and the anchoring crowded out simpler concrete issues the human/Copilot reviewers actually flagged. As a result it MISSED two clusters the baseline caught: (1) the Auto horizontal scrollbar being non-interactive (GT 2/7/12/14) and (2) the CsWin32 dependency/version justification (GT 4/13) -- baseline #14 explicitly asks to justify/document why CsWin32 is needed, mirroring GT, whereas candidate #12 only reframed CsWin32 as a multi-arch build-verification task, which is a different (non-GT) concern and earns no credit under equal rigor. Neither review caught off-screen-offset magnitude (GT 1/5/9), stale selection text (GT 3/8), or the unused-parameter rename (GT 6/11). Harm observed: the cheat-sheet induced topic-anchoring / speculative 'verify that...' comments rather than direct defect calls, lowering both raw (1 vs 3) and distinct (1 vs 3) recall against real reviewer comments.
